newsitem.title: USA: ELEVEN OLYMPIANS NOMINATED FOR JESSE OWENS AWARD. [CORRECTED 21:27 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ELEVEN OLYMPIANS NOMINATED FOR JESSE OWENS AWARD. [CORRECTED 21:27 GMT]

text.p: Eleven 1996 Olympic gold medallists, four of them in swimming and three in athletics, have been nominated for the 1997 Jesse Owens International Trophy Award, International Amateur Athletic Association president Edwin Moses announced on Monday.

American Michael Johnson, the first man to take Olympic gold in both the 200 and 400 metres, the 200 with a world record, could also become the first two-time Jesse Owens award winner, having received it this year. The 1997 award will be presented on February 4 in New York.
(Corrects to make clear that Johnson's win in the 400 metres was not a world record).
Canadian Donovan Bailey, who set a 100 metres world record in Atlanta, and Marie-Jose Perec of France, women's 200 and 400 metres winner, were the other athletics stars nominated.

The swimmers nominated were Penelope Heyns of South Africa, the 100 and 200 metres breaststroke gold medallist; Aleksandr Popov of Russia, 50 and 100 metres freestyle winner; triple gold medallist Michelle Smith of Ireland, 400 freestyle, 200 and 400 individual medley; and quadruple gold medallist Amy Van Dyken of the United States, 50 freestyle, 100 butterfly and 4x100 freestyle and medley relays.
Two Chinese were nominated, diver Fu Mingxia and gymnast Li Xiaoshuang.
Also nominated were Cuban boxer Felix Savon and Turkish weightlifter Naim Suleymanoglu.
The Jesse Owens award is presented to the athlete who best personifies excellence in athletic performance and promotes sincere cooperation and understanding among peoples of all nations.
